The problem with systemd, though is that when it misbehaves, it's not as visible to the end user as problems with Pulse Audio were/are. When Pulse Audio misbehaves, you lose your sound or something else happens.

When systemd misbehaves, well, these are the types of problems you deal with: http://blog.beyondtrust.com/zd_threat/systemd-multiple-vulnerabilities

Take a look at the places where systemd can fail: https://systemdexploit.wordpress.com/ Things like system logging, network communication, etc. Some time ago, (I can't find the link right now), there was an exploit where someone could log into your computer via terminal or ssh, break the systemd system logging so it stops recording what happens, do whatever they want, and the owner of the computer has no trace of them ever doing anything in their logs because logs were broken. And sadly from the video I watched, it was trivial to do, you basically just edited the binary logs directly and they would become corrupted and useless.

It is a mess, it's going to be a very long, rough road before those kind of situations are resolved with systemd given Pulse Audio and Poettering's history.
